summary: The note compares how tech startups in Stockholm and Helsinki are funded through venture capital, angel investing and crowdfunding, plus government initiatives. Stockholm has larger VC volume and a bigger angel pool, while Helsinki is research-focused, close-knit and more measured on crowdfunding. Experts expect more cross-border investment as remote work reduces the importance of location.
one_line: Comparison of venture capital, angel investing, crowdfunding and government support for tech startups in Stockholm and Helsinki, with a view of future trends.
key_facts: Stockholm-based startups have raised more than EUR1 billion since September 2023.
Stockholm's tech sector has attracted international venture capital since the success of companies such as Spotify and Klarna.
Andreas Johansson declared in November 2023 that the Stockholm tech ecosystem offers venture capitalists a unique blend of advanced technologies, innovative business models and skilled entrepreneurs.
Mediflow, a Helsinki digital health startup, secured a EUR20 million investment round in early 2024 from a consortium.
Helsinki startups have smaller investment volume than Stockholm's but focus intensely on research and development, especially health tech and cleantech.
The Finnish Venture Capital Association reported an increase in venture capital investment into Helsinki and praised its collaborative ecosystem bridging academia and industry.
Stockholm Angels pools resources of seasoned entrepreneurs such as Lena Olving and Johan Stael von Holstein to support startups.
The Helsinki Angels Network was founded by Jukka Pekka Makinen, and Helsinki has launched tax incentives for angel investors.
In January 2024, EkoGadget, a tech hardware startup, raised SEK 10,000,000 through a crowdfunding campaign on the Stockholm scene.
FundedByMe is a fixture of Stockholm's startup scene, while in Helsinki crowdfunding is more a supplement; Invesdor combines crowdfunding with traditional investment.
The Swedish government runs the Stockholm Innovation Scholarship, which rewards and finances promising local startups.
The Finnish government implemented Business Finland, offering funding and internationalization services to innovative startups, along with substantial R&D incentives.
Tech analyst Sofia Lundberg predicts cross-border investments between the two ecosystems will become more common.
